transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (BlueOak), Marcus Green (BlueOak), Priya Rao (BlueOak)

---
Summary/Context: POC week 3 check-in. BlueOak is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for payments fraud detection inference (batch & low-latency scoring). This call focuses on sizing, autoscale behaviour during short bursts, and cost tradeoffs for reserve burst nodes vs rapid scaling.
Shared artifacts: https://drive.company/blueoak/redwood/benchmarks - "burst-tests-v3" spreadsheet; policy draft link: docs.redwood/autoscale/sample-policy-v2.json (shared in chat)

Topics:
- Last week's synthetic load results (60s and 30s bursts)
- Observed cold-starts and KV cache priming latency
- Autoscale policy options: target GPU util, queue-depth, pre-warm nodes, burst reservation
- Node flavor discussion (A100-80GB vs H100-80GB), cost and cold-start differences
- Next steps and who runs what tests

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: okay, let's get started, thanks everyone for joining on a friday afternoon, um quick agenda recap - diego will run through the latest burst readouts, then we want to talk policy options, and wrap with next steps.
[00:22] Diego: cool, i'll share my screen, um so this is the "burst-tests-v3" sheet, test-4 was the 60 second burst at 1.8x baseline qps, test-5 was a 5 minute sustained at 1.2x - we saw p50 around 140ms but p95 spiky up to 760ms in the 60s bursts.
[00:45] Marcus: right, important note, those 60s spikes correspond to cold-priming of the kv cache, we noticed the first 5-8 requests per model shard hit disk. that pushed p95 way up.
[01:10] Lena: also, we had a network hiccup mid-test, packet drops on the nic during the second half, which may skew the p95. logs attached in the sheet, prom traces.
[01:32] Diego: agreed; isolating variables is messy but two things jumped out: (1) scale-up latency — we configured minNodes=2, maxNodes=12, scaleUpCooldown=60s, scaleDownCooldown=300s, targetGPUUtil=0.7; with that, scale up took ~48s to add the second node and another ~35s to shift traffic, so very short bursts still stressed the existing nodes, (2) KV cache priming: default cache policy treats new model shards as cold. we can pre-warm or persist cache to avoid this.
[02:05] Priya: from security side, pre-warm means we save cache state across node replacement, does that impact data residency or persistence requirements? we need to review encryption in transit-at-rest for cache snapshots.
[02:28] Maya: short answer: we can encrypt snapshots with customer KMS, and snapshots live in your VPC subnet if you're on private; i'll loop in security doc. but good call priya, we'll include that in the checklist.
[02:45] Marcus: can you unpack the scaling metrics? you mentioned queue-depth as an alternative to pure GPU util?
[03:00] Diego: yeah so targetGPUUtil=0.7 is simple but reacts only after utilization passes threshold. queue-depth triggers earlier: e.g., scale if requestQueue > 40 requests or avg queue wait > 120ms. combined policies work best — we propose a hybrid policy: minNodes=2, prewarmReserve=1, maxNodes=14, scaleUpCooldown=45s, scaleDownCooldown=240s, policy = OR(targetGPUUtil>0.7, requestQueue>45), and an early pre-warm trigger for anticipated scheduled bursts.
[03:45] Lena: prewarmReserve=1 sounds good, does prewarm increase cost immediately? how do we show delta in the cost sheet?
[03:58] Diego: yes it does, it's effectively a reserved node with low-util; in the cost sim i added a "prewarm" row showing +12% monthly cost at our projected baseline. but it reduces p95 spikes for short bursts dramatically — in test-4 with prewarm enabled p95 dropped from 760ms to 220ms on the same workload.
[04:28] Maya: practical question — do we recommend reserving burst capacity (dedicated burst pool) or rely on fast autoscale? which is more predictable for you?
[04:40] Marcus: predictability is huge for us because of SLA to merchants. i'd rather pay a little extra to guarantee latency during the busiest 90th percentile periods. but we'd like to quantify that.
[04:58] Diego: operational tradeoff: reserved burst gives consistent tail latency but costs baseline; autoscale faster helps cost but you might still see short tail blips if bursts < scaleUpCooldown. our hybrid approach + prewarm tends to get the best of both worlds.
[05:20] Priya: i also want to flag compliance — how long do cache snapshots persist? do we rotate keys? KMS integration will need rotation policies.
[05:35] Maya: yes, we support KMS and HSM policies; we'll include retention windows in the security follow-up.
[05:42] Diego: another interesting datapoint: node type mattered. A100 nodes had slightly longer model load times vs H100 in our internal tests — H100 cold-start ~12s, A100 ~18s. that matters for very short bursts. cost per hour for H100 is higher but if you reduce p95 spikes you may net save.
[06:10] Marcus: can you show the cost-per-1M tokens for both flavors?
[06:16] Diego: sure — in the sim: A100 baseline: ~$42 per 1M tokens (including infra amortized), H100: ~$61 per 1M tokens. with prewarm + fewer tail retries H100 scenario's effective user-facing cost per successful inference dropped by about 8% in one sample.
[06:40] Lena: to be honest, our product team will push back on +50% cost. can we tune model quantization to reduce GPU memory and keep H100 off the table?
[06:55] Diego: absolutely, we can recommend int8 quantization profile for your model family. that decreases memory footprint and cold-start time slightly; but quantization changed some edge-case outputs — we should run end-to-end evals.
[07:15] Maya: ok key decisions for this week: (1) try hybrid policy with prewarmReserve=1 and queue-depth trigger, (2) run 60s and 5m bursts again with prewarm enabled, (3) test an int8 quantized model variant in parallel.
[07:35] Marcus: runs agreed. i'll schedule the 5m burst for tuesday and will attach prometheus + node exporter + redis traces.
[07:46] Lena: small ask — can redwood provide a sample prometheus job config for collecting the right metrics? i don't want to miss GPU scheduling metrics.
[07:58] Diego: yup we'll share a prom job and a grafana dashboard link, it's in the shared artifacts as "prom-job-sample.yml".
[08:10] Priya: and security-wise we'll need the SOC2 summary and any penetration testing notes for the Dedicated control plane access.
[08:21] Maya: noted, i'll send the SOC2 summary and coordinate a security PM intro.
[08:28] Diego: one caveat: short scale-up events create transient imbalances when KV cache is warm in one node — we'll recommend sticky routing for 10s after scale events to avoid thrash.
[08:42] Marcus: sticky routing could help, but does that add complexity with canary rollouts?
[08:48] Diego: it's optional; we can scope it as a policy flag per-route. for canaries we can disable sticky.
[08:56] Lena: i want to capture acceptance criteria for the POC: p95 <= 350ms for 60s bursts at 1.8x baseline, no SLA violations for 5m sustained at 1.2x baseline, and clear cost delta documented.
[09:12] Maya: good acceptance criteria, i'll note that.
[09:20] Diego: to avoid confusion, i'll publish updated policy JSON in the drive (docs.redwood/autoscale/poc-blueoak-policy.json) with comments explaining each field.
[09:30] Marcus: last question — if we choose reserved burst nodes, what's the minimum commitment period? monthly or quarterly?
[09:38] Maya: for Dedicated burst reservations we typically offer monthly or annual; monthly is available as a committed sku with 30 day minimum. we'll have the pricing addendum in the follow-up email.
[09:48] Lena: thanks.
[09:51] Maya: wrap up — next steps as we outlined and we'll reconvene next week same time unless you want earlier.
[09:59] Marcus: next week works. thanks everyone.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels and a few words garbled (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache) due to auto-transcribe.
